# [TASK] TMDB-shaped movie endpoints with read-through/save-through (movie-service)

## Task
Implement TMDB v3-shaped movie/genre endpoints in movie-service, with read-through/save-through so cached, persisted, and live responses are indistinguishable to the client.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All TMDB v3 movie/genre endpoints implemented — genre list, movie-by-category (popular/top_rated/upcoming), discover, search, movie detail (`append_to_response` honored), recommendations, similar — [`TmdbFacadeController`](../blob/main/backend/movie-service/src/main/java/com/filmpire/movie/facade/TmdbFacadeController.java)
- [x] Read-through/save-through: Redis -> MongoDB -> rate-limited TMDB -> save -> respond; `page`/`total_pages`/`total_results` preserved exactly as TMDB returns them
- [x] Recorded real-TMDB fixtures replayed through the service produce identical JSON
- [x] Second identical request makes zero further TMDB calls (WireMock call-count assertion)
- [x] Existing native `/api/v1` endpoints still work, all tests green

## Estimate
**Hours:** 10

## Notes
Original design (ADR-003) stored raw TMDB JSON verbatim with short/long Redis TTLs. Superseded by ADR-010: a typed, persisted `Movie` catalog instead, and a flat 5-minute Redis TTL as an L1 cache in front of MongoDB rather than a freshness window. The acceptance criteria above (byte-shape compatibility, zero repeat TMDB calls) hold under the new design too.
